note: Reviewed precision contracts for seven provider families. Each `grammar` is a reference regular expression over the credential itself; `scripts/audit-precision-contracts.py` wraps it in the shared boundary rule (no `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` byte immediately before or after) when it evaluates a fixture. The grammar is an evidence oracle for review, not a runtime detector: the Rust core stays the only authoritative implementation. `basis` records whether a property comes from provider documentation (`provider`), from agreement between the pinned tool sources (`tool-agreement`), from one tool source only (`single-tool`), or from this project's own support policy (`support-policy`). A support-policy property is a choice this project makes and can revisit; it is never presented as provider evidence.

evidenceTiers.T2: no provider documentation for the property; pinned tool sources corroborate it
evidenceTiers.T3: project policy, not a format claim

selectedApproach.summary: Refine the default provider rules in place so they enforce the reviewed contract. No strict mode, no new public option, no new detector id, no finding-type or result-interface change.
alternativesRejected: A separate strict mode or option: splits the corpus into two truths, leaves the default rule broad, and adds public surface for a precision problem that the default rule caused.
Reclassifying the twins as policy cases: hides the false alarms instead of removing them; reclassification never counts as a detector improvement (issue #367).

boundary.rule: A candidate is rejected when the byte immediately before its first byte or immediately after its last byte is in the boundary alphabet. This is beta.4's existing `pattern::boundary_ok` rule and is unchanged by the contracts.

Issue #486 (2026-09-20) re-checked every avenue its own text names and found none resolved: the live `token-formats` and `keys` provider pages still state only the generic `[checksum]` placeholder, with no width or alphabet, for all three prefixes; trufflehog's `cloudflareapitoken` v2 detector at its latest tagged release (v3.97.5, superseding the pinned v3.97.4) still excludes `k` from its `cf[ua]t_` alternation (`trufflehog-3.97.5`); gitleaks' `gitleaks.toml` at its latest tagged release (v8.30.1, unchanged) still has no `cfk_`-specific rule and its `cloudflare-global-api-key` rule still targets only the legacy unprefixed key; GitHub's supported-secret-scanning-patterns page lists a `Cloudflare Global User API Key` partner type (existence only, `github-secret-scanning-patterns` already records this establishes no grammar). No direct correspondence with Cloudflare's docs/security team was sought or available to this review. With none of the three resolving avenues met, issue #486 is closed as won't-fix per the same honest-alternative policy already applied to DigitalOcean's `dop_v2_` and Slack's legacy prefixes: `cfk_` stays permanently unsupported (T1: existence is provider-documented; the checksum shape stays T0 and unscored) until a future provider documentation update states the checksum shape explicitly or a tool ships a `cfk_`-specific rule.

The provider says a checksum follows the 40-character body but does not publish its width or alphabet; the 8-byte lowercase-hex form comes from one tool. A token whose trailing eight bytes are not lowercase hex is intentionally unsupported under this choice.

families.beta4Rule: Not one of issue #367's seven frozen families. The default rule has been `AIza` plus an exact 35-byte suffix from `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` since the detector's introduction, already an exact-length grammar rather than beta.4's shared 20-byte minimum. Issue #487 (this entry) evaluates Google's three OAuth credential formats for coverage and leaves the `AIza` contract unchanged.

toolRules.gitleaks-8.30.1: gcp-api-key: `\b(AIza[\w-]{35})(?:[\x60'"\s;]|\\[nr]|$)` — exact 35-byte body, alphabet `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`; no rule of any kind for `GOCSPX-`, `1//`, or `ya29.`
toolRules.trufflehog-3.97.4: googlegemini: `\b(AIzaSy[A-Za-z0-9_-]{33})` — a narrower 6-byte `AIzaSy` prefix plus 33 bytes, the same 39-byte total length as gitleaks' 4-byte-prefix-plus-35 rule. googleoauth2: `\b(ya29\.(?i:[a-z0-9_-]{10,}))(?:[^a-z0-9_-]|\z)` — open-ended minimum length, no ceiling. No rule for `GOCSPX-` or `1//` in any of this tag's four Google/GCP detector packages (`gcp`, `gcpapplicationdefaultcredentials`, `googlegemini`, `googleoauth2`); `gcpapplicationdefaultcredentials` only extracts an already-present `client_secret` JSON field value contextually, which is not a lexical grammar for the bare, dotenv, or log-line surfaces issue #487 reports as undetected.

pending.reason: Issue #487. No consulted source corroborates a body grammar. Google's own OAuth 2.0 protocol page (reobserved 2026-09-20) shows no example value or format detail for any OAuth credential, only unrelated size ceilings that do not by themselves distinguish a real credential from an arbitrary string of the same size. Neither pinned tool registers a `GOCSPX-` rule at all: gitleaks 8.30.1's only Google rule is `gcp-api-key` (the `AIza` shape above); trufflehog 3.97.4 ships four Google/GCP detector packages and none matches a bare `GOCSPX-` value — `gcpapplicationdefaultcredentials` only extracts a value already sitting in a `client_secret` JSON field once `{...client_secret...}` structure and the `.apps.googleusercontent.com` keyword are present, contextual extraction rather than a lexical grammar, and it cannot help the bare, dotenv, or log-line surfaces this issue reports as undetected. flare-redact 1.6.1 ships `google_api_key` and `gcp_refresh_token` but no `GOCSPX-` rule of any kind. The one signal that exists is GitHub's secret-scanning partner-pattern listing, which names a Google OAuth Client ID type that also lists `google_oauth_client_secret`, with push protection enabled — existence corroboration only, the identical reading this file already applies to Cloudflare's `cfk_` (`families.cloudflare-token.pending`). Freezing a grammar here would be a guess, not a reviewed contract, so `GOCSPX-` is not adopted. If a future gitleaks or trufflehog release ships a `GOCSPX-`-specific rule, or Google's own documentation states the body's length or alphabet, this disposition should be revisited.

Issue #487. The only rule any consulted source ships is flare-redact 1.6.1's `gcp_refresh_token`: `1//[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,160}` — a bare 3-byte prefix plus a 20-to-160-byte minimum-to-maximum run of a common alphabet, single-tool and not independently corroborated by gitleaks (no rule) or trufflehog 3.97.4 (no `1//`-specific rule anywhere in its four Google/GCP detector packages). This is the same broad prefix-plus-minimum-length shape issue #367 found flags near-miss twins across seven other families; adopting a range this wide as a body grammar would reproduce that risk rather than establish a reviewed contract. Google's own OAuth 2.0 protocol page states an upper bound only (refresh tokens ≤512 bytes total) and shows no example value, so it corroborates neither this nor any narrower range. GitHub's secret-scanning partner-pattern listing names a Google OAuth Refresh Token type (push protection enabled) — existence only, the same reading as `GOCSPX-` above. Not adopted; left undetected and recorded, matching how this file already handles DigitalOcean's `dop_v2_` and Slack's legacy prefixes.

Issue #487. trufflehog 3.97.4's `googleoauth2` package registers exactly one rule, for this prefix: `\b(ya29\.(?i:[a-z0-9_-]{10,}))(?:[^a-z0-9_-]|\z)` — an open-ended minimum length (10-byte floor, no ceiling) over a common alphabet, corroborated by no other consulted source: gitleaks has no rule, and flare-redact 1.6.1 has no `ya29.` rule (only `google_api_key` and `gcp_refresh_token`). An open-ended minimum is a weaker shape than even `1//`'s bounded range above and carries the identical near-miss risk issue #367 already documented for bare-prefix-plus-minimum-length grammars. Google's own OAuth 2.0 protocol page states an upper bound only (access tokens ≤2048 bytes total) and shows no example value. GitHub's secret-scanning partner-pattern listing names a Google OAuth Access Token type (push protection enabled) — existence only. `ya29.` tokens are also short-lived by design, which lowers the value of detecting them even if a grammar existed. Not adopted; left undetected and recorded.
